correctness.rationale: Direct line-coordinate change of variables (p,theta,s,u) has pair Jacobian |s-u|. For every line intersecting the translated hole, the blocked ordered endpoint pairs lie across its two surviving segments, and their weighted integral is 2[(L-h)^2-e^2 sin²theta](L+h). Integrating signed q=p-e cos(theta) over [-a,a] and angle gives exact blocking probability with normalization π²(1-a²)². Differentiation at e=0 under the integral gives the analytic second-order integrand; its elementary antiderivatives total -5a sqrt(1-a²), implying b(a,z)=b(a,0)+[5a/(π(1-a²)^{3/2})]|z|²+O_a(|z|^4) and Hessian 10a/(π(1-a²)^{3/2})I. Odd terms vanish by rotational symmetry, with fixed-a analyticity (not uniform near endpoints). Independently compared midpoint/angle quadrature slopes at a=0.2,0.5,0.8, agreeing to better than 5e-6; computation corroborates analytic proof.
